motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that Council instruct the Emergency Management Department, in coordination with the Bureau of Engineering, Bureau of Sanitation, Department of Recreation and Parks, Department of Water and Power, Police Department, and Fire Department, to present at the next Ad Hoc Committee for LA Recovery on their preparations for the super El Nino predicted by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, including but not limited to: • Preparations to fortify low-lying coastal areas against storm surges and flooding, including the City’s fishing piers; • Emergency notifications, evacuation planning and provision of temporary shelter; • Measures to clear catch-basins, debris basins and storm drains to prevent obstructions and create additional capacity for debris and water flow; • Efforts to stabilize hillsides and protect roadways against mud and debris flows in the Palisades bum scar. The presentation should also address other hillside areas at increased risk for mud and debris flows; • Tactics to address and manage overgrown vegetation in Fire Hazard Severity Zones as a result of a wetter winter. — PRESENTED BY: Rk SECONDED BY: TRACI PARK Councilwoman, 11th District Al/G 2 1 2026
title: El Nino / Emergency / Planning / Preparations / City Department Efforts

requests.asks: Prepare presentation on preparations for the super El Nino predicted by NOAA, including fortifying coastal areas, emergency notifications, clearing catch-basins, stabilizing hillsides, and addressing overgrown vegetation in Fire Hazard Severity Zones.
